The Green Clan's new home

Setting

The Green Clan’s new home preserves the Woodsfolk presence on Ingos. Grey Leaf supplies memories of Brissen and clues for the investigation, while elder Khabburu’s requests express a concern for freedom extending even to captive animals. [1, 2, 3]

Two magicians on Ingos

Kir and Kel seek magical help on Ingos. Karansul complains about Yam-Akara, whose cheap runes undercut his trade, and identifies Rinas as the governor’s court magician. His receives the travellers with suspicion and later asks them to retrieve materials from his laboratory. Sver the Trapper offers another route: contact Grey Leaf through the Sacred Flower and a vessel from his cache. Grey Leaf explains that the knight Brissen and his magician friend have left for the settlement near the mines. Kir’s first task here is finding an informed ally, before the murder that later dominates the investigation. The vessel Sver asks them to carry is for Woodsfolk balm that eases his own aching joints. He has used their necessary visit to obtain a personal favour. [4, 5, 6, 2, 7, 8, 9]

Grey Leaf and the poisoned river

Grey Leaf reports that animals are dying after drinking from the northern river. His healers cannot save them while Karansul’s factory keeps discharging poison into the water. Kel recognises that treating the animals alone cannot solve the problem. Karansul proudly confirms his ownership and describes a blasting powder used in his mines. Kir can obtain the powder and destroy the polluting works. Grey Leaf thanks him for ending the contamination. This request concerns the Woodsfolk’s protection of the forest, separately from the search for the Joon artifact. [10, 11, 12, 13]

Crooked’s confession

The settlement’s missing communal money supplies the decisive motive. Kir and Kel catch Crooked at his cache. Brissen had discovered the theft, so Crooked killed him. He also stole His’s knife and the gold nugget, informed on the caravan raid and later planted the knife to shift suspicion. His called the same informant to clear his own name; Crooked mistook that invitation for a trap and killed him too. Woodsfolk observations help reconstruct the planted evidence. Before the governor, Kir explains the connected crimes and Crooked admits them. Yam-Akara is released, while the governor reserves Crooked’s punishment for trial. Kel draws the thief out by spreading word that they have found the hidden money. Afterwards the travellers return the recovered communal funds to Geraldine and Trickster. Geraldine wants personal revenge, but Crooked is already in the governor’s custody. [14, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19, 20]
